header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Delta Labs CTO), Sara Kline (ML Eng), Tomás Ruiz (SRE)
Recording: yes
summary: Initial PLG quickstart discovery for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Delta Labs is evaluating quick time-to-first-token for self-serve API, free credits to prototype, and whether to start on hosted before moving to Dedicated/Private for compliance. Key concerns: latency vs cost, data residency, KMS integration, and benchmark reproducibility.
topics: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE. Priya our SE is on as well. 
[00:08] Mark Chen: Hi all, Mark here, thanks. We just wanna understand how fast we can get something running, and what the path looks like if we then need dedicated capacity or private deployment.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Hi! quick note I work on latency and deployables at Redwood. We'll cover quickstart first then dive into dedicated/private concerns.
[00:28] Sara Kline: quick question up front — what's the typical time-to-first-token for your hosted API? We wanna prototype asap.
[00:34] Jamie Ortiz: For our hosted API most teams get first tokens within minutes, sign up, use free credits, run the quickstart CLI or the SDK. You can do a simple generate call in under 10 minutes if you have a prompt ready. 
[00:47] Tomás Ruiz: minutes, good. We're worried about rate limits and quotas though. For our internal tests we do like 100 tps sometimes.
[00:54] Priya Nair: Right — hosted PLG is meant for low friction dev and early POCs. Quotas for free tier are modest but we can provision larger trial credits for benchmark runs. If you hit production requirements we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
[01:16] Mark Chen: ok, cost vs latency — how much control do we get over batching, kv cache, quantization etc on hosted?
[01:24] Jamie Ortiz: On hosted you get sensible defaults and some tunables via the API (batch window, model variant). For deeper kernel/quantization controls and instance pinning that's where Dedicated or Private comes in. There's also Redwood Optimize suggestions that recommend batching/quant profiles based on workload.
[01:42] Sara Kline: Is the Optimize tool part of the console? Can it suggest specific quantization like int8 or 4-bit?
[01:50] Priya Nair: Yes it's in Console. It recommends quantization profiles and caching strategies; for full control of quantized runtime you'd want Dedicated or Private where you can choose the exact runtime config.
[02:04] Mark Chen: security — we have to do SOC2 and keys are managed by our KMS. Can you integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[02:13] Jamie Ortiz: Absolutely, Private deployments support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Dedicated we also support KMS integration via our enterprise controls, and we provide audit logs and RBAC. We can share SOC 2 docs after this call.
[02:30] Tomás Ruiz: And VPC peering? We need strict networking.
[02:34] Priya Nair: VPC peering or private control plane is supported in Private mode; Dedicated can also be deployed in a VPC with restricted egress depending on your contract. We'll send the network checklist.
[02:46] Mark Chen: What's the typical timeline if we start with hosted and then want to migrate to Dedicated?
[02:52] Jamie Ortiz: Many customers start on hosted (fast iteration) then move to Dedicated once they validate models and traffic. Migration timelines vary but 4-8 weeks is common for a basic migration, more for on-prem/private. We'll help with model pinning and rollouts so you don't get version drift.
[03:10] Sara Kline: For benchmarking — we want to run 1k token contexts at about 30 req/s and see p99 latency. Can you help us reproduce results?
[03:18] Priya Nair: Yes we can provide a benchmark harness and we can run a dedicated trial with increased credits and a reserved test window. We'll need a sample dataset and the prompt set.
[03:30] Mark Chen: Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI and also considered self-hosting. We care about total cost and observing unit economics.
[03:39] Jamie Ortiz: Understood — Redwood tries to make unit economics transparent with token-level cost breakdowns in Console and suggestions on batching and cache to reduce cost.
[03:51] Tomás Ruiz: Any gotchas for large context sizes? We often do long docs summmary, 4k-8k tokens.
[03:58] Priya Nair: The runtime has optimizations for long sequences (KV cache management, attention kernels). For very long contexts we recommend variants optimized for memory and enabling prefix caching. On Dedicated you can tune compilation kernels further.
[04:16] Mark Chen: Can we try the quickstart now? I'm free to test something during this call.
[04:20] Jamie Ortiz: Sure, we can walk through sign up — the quickstart flow: sign up, get API key, install CLI or use curl, run sample generate, see tokens. Do you have a laptop ready?
[04:30] Mark Chen: yep I do.
[04:32] Jamie Ortiz: I'll paste the quickstart link in chat after. The free credits show up in your console within a few minutes. Typical hiccups: corporate SSO may block sign up, or firewall egress to Redwood endpoints; if that happens we can set up a guided onboarding.
[04:48] Sara Kline: How are rate limits surfaced? We need to simulate burst traffic.
[04:54] Priya Nair: Rate limit headers are included in responses; Console also shows token usage and per-route metrics. For bursts we have burst capacity and autoscaling policies on Dedicated.
[05:06] Mark Chen: About data retention and logs — we must not retain PII from our users. What's Redwood's default?
[05:13] Jamie Ortiz: Hosted default is short retention for telemetry but for any regulated workload you'd use Private or a Dedicated plan with stricter retention and the ability to disable logging. We'll include the retention and logging docs.
[05:26] Tomás Ruiz: Ok. On the migration side, do you support A/B rollouts and automatic fallback if a variant is overloaded?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary and A/B rollouts and fallback policies. You can route by latency, cost, region, etc.
[05:44] Mark Chen: For the quickstart, is there an example repo? We wanna embed in our CI to smoke test.
[05:50] Jamie Ortiz: Yep we have a quickstart GitHub repo and CI examples. I'll send the link. It includes an SDK snippet, cURL, and a GitHub Action for smoke testing token budgets.
[06:02] Sara Kline: Are embeddings part of the free credits? We need to try metadata search as well.
[06:07] Jamie Ortiz: Yes the free credits cover generation and embeddings. Embedding unit pricing may differ but you can use credits to test.
[06:15] Mark Chen: Any limitations on model selection for the trial?
[06:19] Priya Nair: You get access to a curated catalog — some high-end model variants may be gated but we'll make sure you have a representative model for latency/cost test.
[06:30] Tomás Ruiz: We have an internal compliance window — if we decide to go Private we'll need an air-gapped option. Is that on the roadmap?
[06:37] Jamie Ortiz: We have an on-prem package for regulated customers; it requires longer lead time and deeper ops support. It's available but tends to be a multimonth engagement.
[06:49] Mark Chen: For Dedicated pricing, is it flat reserved or usage plus reserved?
[06:54] Jamie Ortiz: Typically it's a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual) that gives you predictable throughput; there are also add-ons and burst options. We'll put sample pricing in the follow-up.
[07:06] Sara Kline: Do you offer SOC2 attestations and penetration test reports?
[07:10] Jamie Ortiz: Yes, SOC2 is available. We'll share the attestation and a security overview PDF.
[07:18] Mark Chen: Ok great. Could you walk us through a quick demo of the SDK call? Even a curl would help.
[07:23] Priya Nair: Sure. Example curl: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-base-1","input":"Summarize this doc"}' — response includes token info, latency headers. Note: some transcripts may show it as rwd-base or rwd-bace in the auto transcript.
[07:46] Tomás Ruiz: Noted. For benchmarking we will need exact model variant names, hardware profile, and kernel settings to replicate.
[07:54] Priya Nair: We'll provide model catalog entries and perf profiles. For Dedicated you can pick GPUs and we can share expected p50/p99 latencies for model variants.
[08:05] Mark Chen: Do you have a public performance dashboard?
[08:08] Jamie Ortiz: Public performance benchmarks exist for curated models. For private or dedicated deployments we provide verified profiles as part of onboarding.
[08:18] Sara Kline: Are there cases where hosted has higher latency than self-hosted?
[08:23] Priya Nair: Hosted is optimized for general workloads; self-hosting or Private with specialized hardware can sometimes beat hosted for certain workloads but you trade off operational overhead.
[08:36] Mark Chen: For the POC success criteria — what should we measure?
[08:40] Jamie Ortiz: Good question. Typically: p99 latency under X ms for your prompt set, cost per 1k tokens under threshold, functional correctness/quality of outputs on evaluation prompts, and seamless rollout path to Dedicated.
[08:55] Tomás Ruiz: We'll share a prompt set and an evaluation rubric.
[08:58] Mark Chen: Timeline — we aim to have a working POC in two weeks, then a benchmark week. Feasible?
[09:04] Priya Nair: Yes starting on hosted we can get you to POC in days; to run a reproducible benchmark within two weeks is realistic if we get your prompts and test harness soon.
[09:16] Jamie Ortiz: I'll email the quickstart link and credits. Priya will coordinate the benchmark window.
[09:23] Mark Chen: Anything else we should prepare?
[09:27] Sara Kline: We'll prepare our prompt set, a small dataset for load tests, and confirm stakeholders.
[09:33] Tomás Ruiz: Also network egress rules — we'll validate outbound to api.redwood.ai.
[09:39] Jamie Ortiz: Great. I'll also include SOC2 and the network checklist.
[09:44] Mark Chen: Thanks — this is helpful.
[09:47] Priya Nair: Quick note: if you hit SSO or SAML sign-up issues we can do an invite flow.
[09:53] Jamie Ortiz: Recap next steps: send quickstart + credits, share security docs, schedule benchmark demo.
[09:59] Mark Chen: Sounds good. Thanks folks.
[10:03] End of recording

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (e.g., "rwd-bace" for "rwd-base", "KV cash" for "KV cache"). Some timestamps approximate.
